newsitem.title: USA: Ford U.S. vehicle profits rise in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Ford U.S. vehicle profits rise in Q4.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday its fourth quarter profit per vehicle from U.S. automotive operations was $765, compared with $235 in the year-ago quarter.

The figure excludes one-time costs for employee separation programs. Ford earned $720 per vehicle in the third quarter of 1996, $650 in the second period and $50 in the first quarter. Ford has previously not released the per-vehicle profit figure for its automotive operations.
Ford's fourth quarter earnings were $1.2 billion, or $0.99 a fully diluted share, including one-time items.
A year ago, Ford reported net income of $660 million or $0.48 a share for the quarter.
Ford said its total marketing costs for the U.S. in the fourth quarter were 6.8 percent of revenues, down from 7.2 percent a year ago.

Unlike Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp, a Ford spokesman said the company will no longer break out its vehicle retail incentive amounts. The company believes total marketing costs as a percentage of revenues, which include advertising and other expenditures, is a more accurate reflection, a spokesman said.
Ford's U.S. total market share rose to 26.2 percent in the quarter from 24.9 percent a year ago. But it fell slightly to 25.2 percent in all of 1996 from 25.6 percent for 1995.
In Europe, Ford's share slipped to 11 percent from 11.2 percent during the quarter. For all of 1996 it fell to 11.8 percent from 12.2 percent.
Fleet sales as a percentage of total sales in the U.S. were unchanged on a quarterly basis at 23 percent, and unchanged at 24 percent for all of 1996 versus 1995.
